category_title: Highly gifted African-American male masking ability for social acceptance
minimal_context: Jimmy is in his English class with his peers and is expected to complete and submit a writing assignment.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Jimmy, we are starting the English writing assignment now. Please get your paper out and begin working.

STUDENT: (Keeps his head down on the desk without taking out any materials)

TUTOR: You need to complete the assignment and turn it in so you can get a grade.

STUDENT: I do the work, I just don't turn it in and sometimes I do it in a different way.

TUTOR: If you have the work done, you should just hand it in right now.

STUDENT: (Scoffs) (Puts his head back down to sleep to drown out the classroom environment, refusing to speak or engage any further while his peers are present)

options.A: Agree with him that he is having a rough time with the English writing assignment, acknowledging his frustration while he keeps his head down on the desk.
options.B: Design a covert avenue for him to submit the English writing assignment. Tell him he can leave his notebook before or after school for review, and it will be returned when peers have left.
options.C: Provide direct verbal encouragement and positive reinforcement regarding the English writing assignment, telling him, 'Don't say you can't do the work, you can,' while his peers are present.
options.D: Ask a follow-up question that links his physical sensation to a potential emotional state regarding the English writing assignment while he keeps his head down.
